pairs.subject: agent-instruction-files
pairs.evidence: src/athena/harness/cli_harness.py:323 The harness launches the user's own `claude`/`codex` binary in a directory a program chose, but its default cwd is the launch directory, despite the comment above saying "Never the repository". Nothing in the context passes a flag that limits which instruction files the child loads, or captures and checks that list, so ancestor and user-level CLAUDE.md files can brief the engine without anyone seeing it.

techniques.evidence: src/athena/harness/cli_harness.py:323 Precondition holds: a program creates a directory and launches an agent CLI in it. Within this context the claim that the engine never runs in a checkout is only a comment (line 322), and the default contradicts it. No --setting-sources/--strict-mcp-config-style bound and no check of the loaded set exist; grep of src for setting-sources, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and CLAUDE.md found none.

src/athena/harness/cli_harness.py:343 The injector compares the freshly composed static half against the one the CLI session was opened with, and drops the session to reopen rather than resume when it changed. A session that has been gone or poisoned is reseeded unresumed with the static half (lines 360-367).

src/athena/harness/hooks.py:9 AGENTS.md's 'The gate is the policy' rule lives as deterministic GateHook/LedgerHook/TruncationHook classes that every dialect calls. rounds.py:237 likewise realizes 'Ledger everything' in code.
src/athena/harness/cli_harness.py:58 The CLI's permission and tool defaults are pinned below the model in argv rather than inherited, and tests/harness/test_cli_harness.py:257 asserts the pin.

src/athena/harness/cli_harness.py:163 Facts about the external CLI that can drift (failure signatures) carry the version and date they were measured against; line 122 says a CLI release can reword them.

pairs.registryProposal: workspace-ancestry-isolation frames 'assert the loaded set' around evaluations and scratch workspaces. A product runtime that spawns the user's own coding CLI as its engine has the same exposure: user-level instruction files plus the user's installed MCP/skill floor enter a session whose prompt the product composed. The technique could name that case explicitly, together with the harness flags that bound it.

pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/src/lib/dev/locate.ts:11 This context's build configs, smoke script and dev inspector neither author, load nor spawn anything an agent instruction file governs. Its only agent-adjacent output is a source location a person pastes into a terminal. Grepping apps/desktop (excluding node_modules) for CLAUDE.md, instruction file, system prompt and cursorrules found no hits, and the context's own files hold no agent/claude/codex/prompt term.
